lesson.menu_desc: Telling your best memory -- past simple with at first / suddenly / in the end -- 31 slides
lesson.subtitle: Lesson 23 -- Telling Stories
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Gabriela Pires | Lesson 23 -- Telling Stories | Alumni by Better
lesson.grammar_point: past simple narrative with time sequencers

listenings.text: I want to tell you what happened to me on my first day in Sao Paulo. At first everything was fine. I took the bus to the school and I sat next to the window. I was very happy. Then I opened my bag and I understood the problem: I forgot my phone at home. No map, no messages, nothing. Suddenly the bus stopped and everybody got off, but I did not remember the name of my street. I was really scared for two minutes. Then an old woman looked at me and she asked, are you lost? I said yes in terrible Portuguese, and she laughed. In the end she walked with me for ten minutes and she took me to my door. It was funny and a little embarrassing, but I remember that day every time I take the bus.

This is my best memory of the trip. At first I did not want to go to the museum alone, because my French was terrible. But that morning I went. I took the subway and I got off at the wrong station. Suddenly I was in a street with no tourists, and I was a little scared. Then something wonderful happened. A man with a guitar started to play, and people stopped and listened. I sat on the floor with them for twenty minutes. I forgot the museum, I forgot my map, I forgot everything. In the end I never saw that museum, but I remember the music and the faces of those people. It was the day I understood that I could be alone in a big city and still be happy.

extra_audio.text: First, you set the scene and you say, at first everything was normal. Next, you say what you did and you say, I took the subway and I got off at the wrong station. After that, you say what changed and you say, suddenly a man started to play the guitar. Then, you say how you felt and you say, I was scared, but then I laughed. Finally, you close the story and you say, in the end I never saw the museum, but I remember the music.
